neighbours.label: a D-initial piece that the context has already announced: the expansion of an acronym containing D ('DMV (Department …'), or a repeated d-word ('dos-à-dos')
fire: The DOT (Department of Transportation) repaved the highway last summer.
Funding came from the DOE (Department of Energy) and two universities.
She works for the DNR (Department of Natural Resources) as a forester.
A permit from the DPW (Department of Public Works) is needed to dig here.
The DHS (Department of Homeland Security) issued new travel rules.
The grant was awarded by DARPA (Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency) in May.
The DOJ (Department of Justice) opened an inquiry into the merger.
The DEC (Department of Environmental Conservation) stocks the lake with trout.
quiet: The FAA (Federal Aviation Administration) repaved the runway last summer.
Funding came from the NSF (National Science Foundation) and two universities.
She works for the EPA (Environmental Protection Agency) as a chemist.
A permit from the city engineer's office is needed to dig here.
The Department of Homeland Security issued new travel rules.
The grant was awarded by NASA (National Aeronautics and Space Administration) in May.
Mr. Dalton drove to Dover to deliver the documents on Monday.
The state wildlife agency stocks the lake with trout.

notes: Card: ' D', 'D', '-d', ' Department', Japanese 'ド'; the output direction suppresses D tokens, so the unit fires on a D and votes against another. Probes: 'DMV (Department' 0.82, "'--dan', help='DAN" 0.84, 'dos-à-dos' 0.83, 'DDP (Dongdaemun Design' 0.40, 'DVD (Digital Video Disc' 0.22; plain D words (Davis, Denver, David, Diana) 0.01, the B analogue of the code example 0.03. Near misses: acronyms without D, and D words with no earlier cue.
